# Gotchas

Incident-specific findings that aren't obvious from reading the code. Check this when working in the area a bullet names; it isn't meant to be read top-to-bottom every session (see `CONTRIBUTING.md` for standing rules that are).

- When adding a REST controller/route in the "backend" app, remember the three global auth guards (`JwtAuthGuard`, `PoliciesGuard`, `RolesGuard`, registered as `APP_GUARD` in `AuthModule`) run on every request, including REST ones — not just GraphQL resolvers. They use `GqlExecutionContext.create(...).getContext().req` to read the request, which resolves correctly for a plain Express HTTP handler only because of an incidental quirk (a 3-argument `(req, res, next)` handler is misidentified as a GraphQL "reference resolver" and `res.req` happens to point back to the real request) — don't rely on that silently; verify new REST routes actually work end-to-end rather than assuming the GraphQL-oriented guards behave. If a route needs different token-validation semantics than `JwtAuthGuard` (e.g. accepting an expired-but-validly-signed token), mark it `@Public()` and apply a dedicated `@UseGuards()` guard that reads the request via `ExecutionContext.switchToHttp().getRequest()` instead.
- Also: register a new REST route's path in `compose.yml`'s Traefik labels (`traefik.http.routers.*`) — only `/graphql` is routed by default, so a new REST prefix is unreachable through Traefik until you add its own `PathPrefix` router.
- When adding an AWS SDK v3 package alongside `@aws-sdk/client-s3` (e.g. `@aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner`), pin it to the exact same resolved release as `@aws-sdk/client-s3` (check `npm ls @aws-sdk/client-s3` for the actual resolved version, not just the semver range) — different AWS SDK v3 releases can carry different internal `@smithy/*` versions whose `Client` base class has structurally incompatible private fields, which fails `tsc` even though both packages satisfy their own semver ranges.
- In a class with `class-validator`/`class-transformer` decorators, when one property's type is another decorated class in the **same file**, declare that other class **above** the class that uses it. TypeScript's `emitDecoratorMetadata` embeds a direct (non-lazy) reference to the type in `Reflect.metadata('design:type', ...)` — this is separate from `@Type(() => X)`'s lazy reference used by class-transformer, and a forward reference here compiles and passes `tsc`/unit tests fine, but throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'X' before initialization` at runtime in the production webpack bundle (`nx build backend --prod`), because classes aren't hoisted. Unit tests didn't catch this (the dev transform behaves differently); only booting the actual production bundle did — worth doing after adding any new decorated DTO/input with a nested class.
- A spec that calls `class-validator`'s `validate()` directly on a decorated class (rather than going through a full Nest app bootstrap) needs `reflect-metadata` imported first — added globally to `apps/backend/vitest.setup.ts` since `main.ts`'s own import of it never runs in unit tests.
- `apps/backend/src/shared/beatrice/schema.graphql` is a checked-in **snapshot** of Beatrice's schema — `gql.tada` generates its types from this local file, not a live introspection query. When Beatrice's real schema gains a field/mutation you need to call, update this snapshot first (copy from `smart-novel-beatrice/docs/schema.graphql`, or fetch live) — otherwise `graphql()` tagged documents referencing the new field won't typecheck, with no clear error pointing at the real cause.
- When bumping `compose.yml`'s `beatrice` image tag, diff `smart-novel-beatrice`'s `src/utils/config.py` (or its `docs/schema.graphql`) between the old and new tag before assuming the compose env block still works — Beatrice has twice shipped a breaking config/contract change on a minor bump with no migration note: 3.1.0 switched `Qwen3TtsProvider` to DashScope's native REST contract (broke the local dev shim's request shape), and 4.1.0 added a `model_validator` requiring `TTS__QWEN__API_KEY` to be non-empty for the default provider even when `TTS__QWEN__BASE_URL` points at the local no-auth `qwen-tts` shim. Both surfaced as the `beatrice` container crash-looping on `docker compose up --wait`, not as a compile-time or unit-test failure.
- Local TTS synthesis needs the `qwen-tts` compose service (vendored under `local-setup/qwen-tts/`, mirroring `smart-novel-beatrice`'s own dev setup) running and `beatrice`'s `TTS__QWEN__BASE_URL` pointed at it — without it, Beatrice's qwen3-tts provider defaults to DeepInfra and every `generateAudio` call fails on `GET /v1/voices -> 401` (no API key configured). Not obvious from the error alone; found only by checking Beatrice's own logs during a live `generateAudio` call.
- When a `REQUIREMENTS.md` step's prose describes a new component (e.g. "a small bridge service") that would duplicate a subscription/connection/map lookup an earlier step already set up, treat that as a description of the _behavior_ to add, not a literal instruction to create a new class — extend the existing owner instead, unless there's a real reason (different lifecycle, different failure domain) to split it out. Surfaced in Step 2.2: the AC described a "bridge service" for re-publishing Redis status updates onto GraphQL `PubSub`, but `ChapterNarrationService` (Step 2.1) already subscribed to that same channel and held the job-to-chapter map; a second subscription would have duplicated both for no benefit.
- `LOG_LEVEL` (`.env`/`.env.example`, default `http`) filters out `.debug()` calls in `CustomLoggerService` — `docker compose logs`/e2e log persistence will show nothing for a `.debug()` line even when that code path ran fine. Before concluding a code path never executed from an absent log line, check it wasn't logged at `.debug()`; `.warn()`/`.error()` aren't filtered and are more trustworthy for "did this run" checks.
- This environment's own memory-pressure monitor kills a long `docker compose up`/`nx e2e` invocation well before real host memory is exhausted — recurred across multiple full `backend-e2e` runs, including once right at the very end after `qwen-tts`'s real synthesis (`python3 server.py`) had grown to several GB RSS, with `free -h` showing tens of GB still available at the moment of the kill. Deliberately passing `run_in_background: true` up front gets killed far more reliably than a plain foreground call the tool auto-backgrounds after its own ~600s cap once already running — prefer the latter. Either way, check the partial log before assuming a killed run failed outright: vitest prints each passed/failed test as it goes, so a kill after the last `✓`/`×` line still tells you the real per-test outcome.
- Real TTS synthesis against the CPU-only local shim under several tests' concurrent load produces polling-timeout failures that move between different tests on each rerun, never the same test twice, and never on incorrect output — that pattern is resource contention, not a regression; confirm by rerunning 2-3 times and, if still unsure, cross-check with an isolated graphql-api-tester call against the dev server.
- In a Prisma `create`, you can't mix a scalar foreign key field (e.g. `novelId`) with a nested relation `create`/`connect` for a _different_ relation (e.g. `content: { create: {...} }`) on the same model — TypeScript picks the `*UncheckedCreateInput` variant as soon as any scalar FK is present, which has no room for a nested relation write, and fails with a cryptic `Type '{ create: ... }' is not assignable to type 'undefined'` pointing at the unrelated field. Fix: express every relation you're nesting into via `relationName: { connect: { id } }` instead of the scalar FK, so Prisma picks the relation-based `*CreateInput` variant. Surfaced in Step 1 (Create Chapter) creating `Chapter` + `ChapterContent` together: `novelId` + `content: { create }` failed; `novel: { connect: { id: novelId } }` + `content: { create }` typechecked.
- A variant that does NOT move between reruns: `beatrice`'s worker taking 190-350s of genuine CPU synthesis before reaching `uploading`, then getting `401 Unauthorized` calling `backend-e2e`'s `/beatrice-callbacks/gen-upload-url` with the token it was issued at job-queue time. `BeatriceTokenGuard`/`verifyIssuedByUs` accepts an expired-but-signed token, so plain expiry alone shouldn't cause this — the actual `jose` failure mode under this delay hasn't been root-caused. Confirmed repeatedly, always the same tests (`chapter-narration.e2e-spec.ts`'s and `beatrice-callbacks.e2e-spec.ts`'s real-pipeline/live-progress tests), never caused by the diff under test — treat as this same CPU-timing environment class whenever the failing tests are the ones that always drive a real multi-minute synthesis and the diff doesn't touch the auth/worker/upload path.
